function: UAV target detection: ResNet-18 regresses per-path micro-Doppler signatures that are clustered to drop multipath false alarms; sensing processing, not beams, waveforms or resources (p. 3).
notes: Excluded for function, the first code that applies. Checks 1-4 pass: an IEEE WCL research letter (p. 1) that proposes and evaluates a method; a ResNet-18 trained on labeled spectrogram-signature pairs (pp. 3-4) processes the received sensing signal, not a decision above the physical layer. The learned task is target sensing, p. 3: "A deep learning model is utilized to extract the UAV micro-Doppler signature given in (1) from the spectrogram"; the signatures are clustered to group the paths of each UAV and keep the shortest one for localization (pp. 3-4). Results are detection and positioning only, p. 4: "The compared metrics were the false alarm rate (FAR), missed detection rate (MDR), and position estimation error". The system is nominally ISAC, p. 4: "The sensing reference signal utilized a frequency comb-4 configuration, while the remaining resources were allocated for communications", so it is not sensing in a system that does not communicate; but the beams (fixed wide-angle beamforming with an 8x8 panel, p. 4), the waveform, and the resources are fixed rather than learned, and no communication metric is reported, so the learned method solves no area 5 problem (beams, waveforms, resources serving sensing and communication) nor that of any other area; UAV identification and localization are excluded functions. Reviewer may confirm this area 5 boundary. The PDF is the paper of the DOI: title and DOI 10.1109/LWC.2025.3581572 on p. 1.
